data_feeds._doc: P6 registry: dashboard/risk data feeds with an expected freshness window and the healer that refills them. Windows span weekends for weekday-cadence feeds. A feed whose stamp is unparseable can never be judged fresh and is always a violation. A feed may also declare 'assert_fields' (dotted path -> not_in / equals / max_count + why) to have its CONTENTS checked: a freshness window only proves the builder ran, and on 2026-07-20..08-11 vol_metrics was rewritten daily with a fresh stamp while five of its nine feeds were dark, so P6 passed every day of a three-week outage.

classification_vocab._doc: L4 registry: canonical enum values per classification field, mirrored from _system/frameworks/classification.md (the prose authority). Sentinels mean 'not yet classified' and are exempt everywhere. Criteria surfaces (personas.json criteria, power_zones.json zone rules and profile preferred_archetypes) may only reference canonical values; data surfaces (valuation.json classification_inputs, portfolio registry) may only carry canonical values or sentinels. L4 also asserts no persona lens is strictly narrower than its own power zone on a shared axis -- the stahl-omits-optionality class.

live_feeds._doc: P7 registry: feeds published through the HMAC ingest rather than committed as files, so the only local evidence they ran is the publisher's own log. evidence_path may be absolute or ~-rooted (machine-local, by design) or repo-relative. P7 is REPORT severity and its skip rule differs from P6's: an evidence file that is ABSENT is SKIPPED with a reason (a CI checkout has no local monitor logs, and an invariant that reddens on every CI run is one everybody learns to ignore), while an evidence file that EXISTS and is stale, or whose stamp cannot be parsed, is a violation. Windows span weekends, as in data_feeds: the flow monitor only publishes when minute bars arrive.
